notes: Dark wood-veneer sheet panelling -- the WAINSCOT on the lower wall of a room finished around 1980 and still there in 1997 (walker, 2026-09-15, card-shop references). The tile is one 4 ft sheet (1.2192 m) carrying 6 score grooves at 8 in on centre, the standard random-plank pitch. The joint is `stripes`' own seam, 6% of a band either side of it, so it is 12% of the 203.2 mm pitch: 24.4 mm, 2.6 texels at the pack's 105 px/m, against a real V-groove of about 6 mm. 6 mm is 0.63 of a texel at this density and cannot be drawn. hardwood_plank does not cover it: that is kind 'wood', a mid-brown FLOOR plank 0.3333 m between joints against this one's 0.2032 m, at roughness 0.407 and with no wear pass of any kind, and a theme holds one grammar per kind -- a card shop needs plank wood on its shelving at the same time as panelling on its wall. Scuffing is IRREGULAR, not floor-anchored: Zoo cube-projects world-metre UVs, so the tile's phase follows the wall's world position and a gradient authored at the bottom of the tile lands at an arbitrary height. A skirting-height scuff belongs to a mesh-aware pass (Patina) or to a separate trim module, not to a tiling texture.
